profile.name: Zhe Jiang (Alex)
profile.intro: I’m a psychology undergraduate at ELTE, working on how the brain represents information and how cognitive states shape sensory processing.
profile.about: My work in collaborative fMRI projects connects research questions with analysis pipelines, model comparisons and visual explanations. At ELTE, I also work on resting-state EEG preprocessing and quality control.

interests.title: Cognitive state

interests.title: Computational methods
interests.description: How can careful modelling and quality control make neural data interpretable?

projects.title: The geometry of cognition
projects.summary: Relating cognitive states through the structure of neural activity patterns.
projects.question: How can we distinguish an overall cognitive state from the particular strategy used to reach it?
projects.approach: The project connects exploratory Isomap embeddings with representational similarity analysis (RSA) and pattern component modelling (PCM). Comparisons in the original pattern space, explicit candidate models and sensitivity analyses help assess the interpretation of a visual map.
projects.contribution: I implement and check representational analyses, compare modelling choices and prepare visual and statistical reports. My work includes examining temporal proximity, input quality and the stability of model comparisons. Interpretation and manuscript development are collaborative.
projects.release: Collaborative research in progress. This overview presents the question and analysis approach; empirical results and manuscript figures remain private.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual coloured point clouds representing a neural pattern space; synthetic coordinates.
projects.motivation: Different strategies can share aspects of cognitive processing. Comparing their neural activity patterns offers a way to ask which relationships reflect shared state and which reflect strategy-specific structure. A low-dimensional map can help us explore these relationships, but its interpretation also depends on noise, sampling and temporal structure.
projects.currentWork: Refining comparisons between candidate accounts of cognitive state, checking sensitivity to analysis choices and integrating these checks into the manuscript.

methodDetails.name: RSA

methodDetails.name: PCM

methodDetails.name: Sensitivity & inference
methodDetails.purpose: Examine temporal structure, input quality and the stability of model comparisons; report uncertainty and multiple-comparison decisions.

projects.title: How we receive information
projects.summary: Examining neural activity across different ways of receiving sensory information.
projects.question: How does the way we receive sensory information change the use of shared neural systems?
projects.approach: Visual and auditory fMRI workflows bring together multivoxel pattern comparisons, representational relationships, hidden-state descriptions and connectivity modelling. These provide different perspectives on sensory information processing; their inputs and assumptions need to be checked separately.
projects.contribution: I contribute to event and time-series alignment, computational workflows, checks across analysis branches and visual reporting. I also help coordinate analysis tasks within the team.
projects.release: High-level project description. Internal conditions, network specifications, analysis outputs and unpublished results remain private.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual state trajectories and network connections, with no empirical measurements.
projects.motivation: Two processing conditions may involve overlapping neural systems while differing in how those systems are used. This project separates questions about shared activity patterns from questions about their changing expression over time and their network interactions.
projects.currentWork: Checking event labels and analysis inputs, reconciling outputs across representation, state and connectivity branches, and integrating the analysis record with the manuscript. Some workflow revisions still require validation.

projects.title: Features, perception & inference
projects.summary: Connecting measurable properties of stimuli with models of brain activity.
projects.question: How can measurable stimulus features inform models of neural responses during perception?
projects.approach: The workflow connects quantitative image descriptors with feature-based fMRI general linear models in SPM. Feature definitions, scaling, event alignment and first- and second-level model specifications form linked parts of the analysis.
projects.contribution: I work on implementing and checking the fMRI modelling workflow, including comparisons between scripted and interactive SPM setups. I contribute to feature preparation, analysis documentation and coordination of analysis tasks within the collaborative project.
projects.release: Methods and responsibilities overview. Stimulus materials, feature tables and neural effect estimates remain private.
projects.imageAlt: An abstract stimulus marker over a feature matrix; illustrative values only.
projects.motivation: Perceptual responses can depend on several properties of a stimulus at once. Describing properties such as colour and texture makes those hypotheses explicit, while feature scaling and model design affect how response estimates can be interpreted.
projects.currentWork: Checking feature definitions and scaling, documenting model inputs and keeping analysis specifications consistent across stages.

methodDetails.name: Image descriptors

methodDetails.name: Feature preparation

methodDetails.name: SPM general linear models
methodDetails.purpose: Link stimulus features and event timing to estimates of neural responses.

methodDetails.name: Workflow checks
methodDetails.purpose: Compare scripted and interactive model setup and document the inputs passed between analysis stages.

projects.title: Making EEG analysis inspectable
projects.summary: Building an inspectable resting-state EEG workflow with human review.
projects.question: How can an EEG preprocessing workflow make each quality-control decision clear and reviewable?
projects.approach: Within the ELTE Music and Language Development Research Group, I work on a resting-state EEG preprocessing workflow in MATLAB and EEGLAB. It covers signal preparation, ICA, channel and epoch inspection, and saved quality-control decisions.
projects.contribution: I implement practical preprocessing steps and quality-control reports, and inspect channels, independent components and epochs. Automatic methods provide review candidates; a human reviewer records the final decisions. I also maintain documentation that connects those decisions to the analysis workflow.
projects.release: Workflow description only. Recordings, participant identifiers, individual quality-control reports and unpublished study details remain private.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic EEG-like traces with a highlighted review window, not participant data.
projects.motivation: Preprocessing choices determine which signals enter a later EEG analysis. Making the evidence and the reviewer’s decisions visible helps collaborators understand how an analysis input was produced and revisit a decision when needed.
projects.currentWork: Improving channel and epoch quality-control reporting, keeping manual decisions traceable and preparing reviewed recordings for later analyses. This page presents preprocessing work; downstream EEG findings are not reported.
